summary: A convincing medieval foundation: the King has clear royal authority, the jester has an excellent silhouette, and the four everyday roles are broadly distinguishable. Revise the modern-looking garment details, strengthen the hoods and mantle, and resolve rigid skirt construction before approval.
problems: The carpenter reads primarily as a belted modern shirt over straight trousers; the fallen hood contributes almost nothing to the visible silhouette.
The breadmaker's two narrow apron straps resemble suspenders, while the solid pale cylinder reads as a disc rather than a bowl or bread.
The elder's disconnected front mantle panels resemble an oversized bow tie rather than a continuous medieval shoulder garment.
The messenger's hood reads as a pointed cap: its neck coverage and trailing hood shape are insufficiently visible.
The breadmaker and elder have long, single hip-bound boxes enclosing both legs. Walking clearance is unproven, with a substantial risk of legs breaking through the rigid garments.

The jester reads immediately as a performer, but the small chest diamond does little to distinguish a visiting court from a local entertainer. Important costume contrasts also depend on unspecified avatar colours.
fix: Carpenter: Make the tunic visibly longer than a shirt, with a stepped or split hem over close-fitting hose. Enlarge the fallen hood into a connected neck-and-shoulder roll with a visible folded tail down the back. Keep the belt and wooden mallet. Breadmaker: Replace the vertical straps with a clear waist-apron tie over the long gown. Fit the linen coif closely around the sides and back of the head. Replace the pale disc with a chunky scored loaf or a shallow bowl with a contrasting recessed interior. Use an articulated skirt or overlapping lower panels that accommodate each leg. Market Elder: Join the front panels across the shoulders to the back mantle, forming one broad, sloping garment rather than two bow-tie tabs; retain one central clasp. Keep the cap and staff, and articulate the long robe for walking. Messenger: Extend the hood around the cheeks and onto the shoulders; lower and tilt its point backwards into a trailing liripipe. Preserve the short tunic, tall boots and satchel, ensuring the strap visibly meets the bag. King: Preserve the crown, sceptre and broad contrasting cloak. Join the cream shoulder pieces into a continuous fur yoke and verify cloak clearance during arm swings and walking. Far-Court Jester: Preserve the three-point bell cap and divided costume. Guarantee strong light–dark separation between its colour halves, enlarge the diamond into a bold visiting-court device, and repeat it on a short shoulder tab visible from above. Check all six outfits on both body variants in walking poses and at actual stream scale.
